skill.name: amazon-customer-review-and-rating-summary-scraper
skill.description: Get Amazon customer reviews and a product-level rating summary by product URL, keyword, or category, with star-rating and sort filters, across 23 Amazon domains. Output fields: productAsin, ratingScore, reviewTitle, reviewDescription, isVerified and more, as JSON rows. Use it for requests like "Amazon review scraper", "Amazon rating summary", "product review export", or a CSV/JSON export of public Amazon data.
skill.summary: Run an Apify Actor to collect public Amazon reviews and rating summaries with discovery, filtering, and marketplace options.
skill.author: bolvein-firex

security_audit.summary: All 82 static alerts reflect documentation syntax or expected CLI file reads, environment configuration, and authenticated Apify requests. One semantic finding identifies optional session-cookie forwarding that contradicts the public-data guardrail and can expose authenticated Amazon access to a third-party Actor. No evidence found of malicious intent or prompt injection in the reviewed files; the remote Actor implementation was not available for review.

remediation.issue: The input schema invites session-cookie submission despite the public-data-only guardrail, and the runner forwards input without rejecting cookies.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookieString from the public-data schema and reject nonempty cookieString values in the runner before any network request.

semantic_findings.title: Session-Cookie Forwarding Conflicts With Public-Data Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The schema requests a "logged-in Amazon session cookie" through cookieString, while SKILL.md says "Do not pass cookies, sessions or private account data." The runner serializes supplied input unchanged to Apify, so this optional field can expose authenticated Amazon session access to a third-party Actor.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The schema explicitly solicits a session cookie, and the runner forwards every parsed input property without filtering. isSecret marks the schema field but does not prevent transmission; no evidence found of automatic cookie collection.

content.user_title: Collect Amazon Reviews and Rating Summaries
content.value_statement: Manual review collection makes product comparisons slow and inconsistent. This skill runs an Apify Actor to collect public Amazon reviews with rating summaries and configurable filters.
actual_capabilities: Submit product URLs or ASINs, or discover products from keywords and Amazon category URLs.
Configure 23 Amazon storefronts and merge additional marketplace reviews through the Actor input.
Request review filters for stars, verified purchases, keywords, dates, and attached media.
Request product rating summaries with average ratings, global rating counts, star histograms, and customer-summary aspects.
Run authenticated synchronous requests through the Node.js helper using a JSON file, inline input, or the bundled example.
Use documented asynchronous API commands to start larger runs, check status, and retrieve dataset rows.
limitations: Requires an Apify account and token; Actor usage is billed, and the Node.js helper requires Node 18 or later.
Scraping runs in an external Actor whose implementation is not included; this package does not independently guarantee remote behavior or output completeness.
Extended review history covers Amazon.com only; availability varies, narrow filters may return no rows, and unparseable review dates remain included.
The helper prints JSON and does not provide native CSV conversion; cookieString must remain unset despite its presence in the reference schema.

use_cases.title: Compare Product Feedback
use_cases.description: Collect public reviews for selected ASINs with consistent star filters and rating summaries before comparing customer feedback.

use_cases.title: Research Category Sentiment
use_cases.description: Discover a limited set of products by keyword or category, then collect recent reviews for a documented market research sample.

use_cases.title: Prepare Repeatable Review Exports
use_cases.description: Run saved input configurations through Apify and retrieve structured datasets for downstream reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Collect a Small Product Sample
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect up to 20 public reviews for [Amazon product URL]. Include rating summaries, exclude reviewer identities, and leave cookieString unset. Confirm Apify costs before running.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: collect reviews for one known product.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Products by Keyword
prompt_templates.prompt: Find two products for [keyword] on [Amazon storefront]. Collect up to 20 reviews per product, sorted by recent, with aggregates. Do not submit cookies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: collect a bounded discovery sample.

prompt_templates.title: Filter Critical Product Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: For [ASINs], request critical reviews from verified purchases mentioning [terms], dated after [YYYY-MM-DD]. Cap each product at 100 reviews. Exclude identities and cookies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a focused feedback dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a Larger Marketplace Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an asynchronous run for [ASINs] across [marketplaces]. Confirm costs, set explicit review caps, exclude cookies and identities, and verify completion before retrieving results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a larger run using the documented API workflow.

This describes the expected dataset structure, not a measured collection result.

best_practices: Start with two discovered products and 20 reviews each; inspect results and Apify pricing before increasing limits.
Leave cookieString unset and includeGdprSensitive false; keep APIFY_TOKEN in the environment and review input files before submission.
Check site terms and applicable law; record marketplace, filters, and collection time when interpreting results.
anti_patterns: Submitting Amazon session cookies, passwords, or private account data to obtain deeper review history.
Treating filtered reviews as a complete or representative sample of all customer opinions.
Starting large paid runs without explicit limits, cost approval, or confirmation that asynchronous processing has completed.

faq.question: Do I need an Apify account?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide APIFY_TOKEN for authenticated requests and review Actor pricing because usage is billed to your Apify account.

faq.question: Can I use keywords instead of product URLs?
faq.answer: Yes. Keywords and category URLs support discovery when productUrls is empty. maxProductsToDiscover limits products found per discovery input.

faq.question: Which Amazon marketplaces are supported?
faq.answer: The schema lists 23 storefronts. Product URLs retain their domain, while country selects the storefront for bare ASINs and discovery.

faq.question: Will I receive every review?
faq.answer: No. Coverage varies by product and public source. Extended history covers Amazon.com only, and filters or review caps can reduce returned rows.

faq.question: Should I provide an Amazon session cookie?
faq.answer: No. Leave cookieString unset to follow the public-data guardrail. The reference schema offers this field, but the runner forwards it to Apify.

faq.question: Does the helper export CSV or handle large runs?
faq.answer: The helper prints JSON through a synchronous endpoint with a documented 300-second limit. Use the asynchronous workflow for larger runs; CSV conversion is separate.
